title: Understanding the dashboard
summary: A warning-light encyclopedia: which lights mean stop now, which mean get it checked, and what happens if you ignore them.

lessons.title: The colour code of warning lights
objectives: Use colour to judge how urgent a warning light is.
Know the lights that mean stop as soon as it is safe.
Tell a bulb check at start-up from a real warning.
lessons.intro: A dashboard can show dozens of symbols, but you do not need to memorise them all at once. Start with the colour: it tells you how urgent the message is. Then learn the handful of red lights that mean stop now.

p: Red: a serious fault or a dangerous condition. Stop as soon as it is safe and switch off, or do not drive until it is sorted. Amber (yellow or orange): something needs attention soon. You can usually continue carefully to a workshop, but find out what it means first. Green or blue: a system is working as intended — headlights on, indicator flashing, cruise control active.

Oil pressure, coolant temperature, brake system, charging (battery), and power steering on some cars are the lights that most often mean stop. A flashing check-engine light also means stop or slow right down: it usually signals a misfire that can overheat and destroy the catalytic converter.

note.text: Stopping safely means signalling, moving off the carriageway, and switching on hazards — not braking hard in a live lane.

p: When you turn the key to ignition (or press start without your foot on the brake), most lights come on for a moment to show the bulbs and systems work. They should go out within a few seconds of the engine starting. A light that does not come on at all during this check may be a fault too — for example, an airbag light that never shows.

terms: The brief self-test when ignition is switched on, during which most warnings light up.
Malfunction indicator lamp — the check-engine light.
examples: The amber TPMS light comes on during a highway drive. Slow down, stop at the next safe place, look at all four tyres, and check pressures at the next fuel station.
mistakes: Covering a persistent amber light with tape or ignoring it for weeks.
Stopping on the carriageway itself when a red light appears.
safety: When in doubt about a red light, do not keep driving. Call roadside assistance.

check.q: An amber warning light usually means:
o: A fault that needs attention soon
The car is in eco mode
check.r: Amber means check it soon. Red means stop safely; green or blue means a system is on.

check.q: The check-engine light is flashing, not steady. What does that usually indicate?
o: A severe misfire — slow down and stop safely
Nothing — it is a bulb test
check.r: A flashing MIL usually means a misfire that can overheat the catalytic converter. Reduce load and get it checked immediately.
